chunk_findings.detail: `live_runs` treats a marker as live only when `m.pid_start` is truthy, but the module’s own `_is_live` helper treats a marker with no recorded start time as live if `alive(m.pid)` is true. Given a running gate-run marker such as `{"pid": 1234, "pid_start": null, "host": "<current-host>"}` (e.g. from an older marker writer or a partial marker), `_is_live` would report it live, but `live_runs` filters it out because of `m.pid_start`. The lease item is then treated as having no live gate run, so the idle clock is not reset and `verdicts`/`judge` can still emit `yield_requested` or allow a break—asking a working agent to yield, which is the bug being fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/running.py:live_runs

chunk_findings.detail: The new live-gate probe is an external dependency on filesystem marker layout and live-process state, but it is invoked directly from `_live_gate` via `ddflow.services.gates.running.live_runs` rather than through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. The regression test compounds this by calling the real `RUN.mark_started(tmp_path, "T1", "ci", sha="abc")` instead of a fake adapter. This violates [r-adapters]: a new port/touch point should isolate such a dependency in `ddflow/adapters`, and tests should use a fake rather than the real filesystem/process state.

chunk_findings.detail: The new marker-slicing logic still does not prove it is examining the actual `RESOURCES` table. It takes the last textual occurrences of `RESOURCES: tuple` and `RESOURCE_BY_URI`, so a comment or docstring after the real table can become the slice. For example, if `_core.py` contains a real `RESOURCES` tuple that has regressed to contain `fold(` or `EventLog`, then later has a line like `# RESOURCES: tuple` before the `RESOURCE_BY_URI = ...` definition, `start` points into that comment and `end` points at the definition; `table = src[start:end]` is just the comment, `assert start < end` passes, and the final assertion passes vacuously. The added `start < end` check only prevents the end marker from being before the start marker; it does not ensure the selected markers are the module-level table and its derived mapping.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py::test_every_mcp_resource_is_served_through_the_cli

chunk_findings.detail: The rindex-based slice is still not anchored to the actual module-level `RESOURCES: tuple` definition, only to the last textual occurrence of the substring. If `_core.py` has a comment or docstring between the real `RESOURCES: tuple` and `RESOURCE_BY_URI` containing exactly `RESOURCES: tuple` (for example `# RESOURCES: tuple is converted below`), then `src.rindex("RESOURCES: tuple")` returns that later comment position, so `table = src[start:end]` excludes the real resource table. The `assert start < end` only ensures a non-empty slice, not that it starts at the actual table. In that input the test passes even when a real `RESOURCES` entry calls `fold(` or references `EventLog`, defeating the regression check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py:312-315

chunk_findings.detail: The new table slice still identifies the `RESOURCES` table only by the last textual occurrences of `"RESOURCES: tuple"` and `"RESOURCE_BY_URI"`, so it can select a comment or docstring instead of the real module-level table. For example, if `_core.py` contains a regressed table such as `RESOURCES: tuple = (fold(...),)` followed by a line like `# RESOURCES: tuple is converted below` and then `RESOURCE_BY_URI = ...`, then `src.rindex("RESOURCES: tuple")` points at that comment and `src.rindex("RESOURCE_BY_URI")` points at the real derivation, so `table` excludes the regressed table and the assertion `"fold(" not in table` passes even though the served resources still fold the log. The added `start < end` check does not prevent this because both markers can occur in non-code text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py::test_every_mcp_resource_is_served_through_cli

chunk_findings.detail: Both previous rindex findings still hold: the slice is anchored to the last textual occurrences of `"RESOURCES: tuple"` and `"RESOURCE_BY_URI"`, not to the actual module-level definitions. For example, if `_core.py` has a real `RESOURCES` tuple that regressed to contain `fold(`, and a later comment such as `# RESOURCES: tuple is converted below` appears before `RESOURCE_BY_URI = ...`, `start = src.rindex("RESOURCES: tuple")` points into that comment. Then `src[start:end]` excludes the real tuple, so `assert "fold(" not in table` passes despite the regression. The added `assert start < end` does not catch this because the comment still precedes `RESOURCE_BY_URI`.

The scenario posits a comment '# RESOURCES: tuple is converted below' that does not exist; adding such a comment would itself be a real change the guard legitimately flags.
